text:
We burned a design review on gRPC vs REST for a URL shortener.

Nobody had written down redirects per second, bytes per row, or read vs write volume. You can't pick a sane architecture until those orders of magnitude exist.

Napkin math isn't spreadsheet precision — it's rounding on purpose: ~100K seconds per day, peak QPS, storage with replication, bandwidth. Wrong exponent beats wrong microservice name every time.

I walked through URL shortener and payment numbers and the mistakes I still make (forgetting peak multiplier, counting browser QPS but not fan-out).
